items.prompt: On Day 1, the class simulated an imagined object using shapes on graph paper. What does it mean to "simulate" an object this way?

choices.A: Copy a photo of it exactly, pixel by pixel
choices.B: Use basic geometric shapes to represent the object's key features
choices.C: Write a paragraph describing the object instead of drawing it
choices.D: Measure the real object with a ruler and stop there

items.rationale: A mathematical model uses simple shapes to capture the important structure of a real object, not an exact copy.

items.prompt: A student draws a backpack using two rectangles and one triangle. This drawing is an example of:

choices.A: An exact replica of the backpack
choices.B: A mathematical model that captures the object's important shapes

items.rationale: Modeling means representing key features with simpler shapes, not creating an exact replica.

items.prompt: Which shape has exactly 4 sides and 4 right angles, by definition?
items.rationale: A rectangle is defined as a quadrilateral with four right angles.

items.prompt: A rectangle used to model a book is 3 units wide and 5 units long on graph paper. How many square units does the rectangle cover?
items.rationale: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 5 x 3 = 15 square units.

items.prompt: Why do mathematicians often use simple shapes instead of exact, detailed drawings to model real objects?

choices.B: Simple shapes make the important structure easier to measure and analyze
choices.C: Detailed drawings are against the rules
choices.D: Simple shapes always take longer to draw

items.rationale: Models simplify reality so the important structure (like size and shape relationships) is easier to work with mathematically.
